Let me also think about whether there's anything else in the protocol I should handle. Let me re-read a couple of paragraphs I might have skimmed:

"## Batch input and directory ... Limits per invocation: 0-2048 jobs, 1-64 gateways, 0-2048 directory identities, at most 8192 explicit aliases and 2048 accounts; each allow/domain list has at most 2048 entries. Any request text longer than 32768 characters rejects with syntax, including a reused forwarded request that grew during normalization. The sum of the request lengths actually processed (including each source reuse) is at most 4 MiB; the complete UTF-8 input JSON is at most 8 MiB. These are supported input bounds, not score or performance targets." ✓

"## SIP framing and headers ... A line beginning SP/HTAB continues the preceding field: replace the line break and the maximal leading SP/HTAB run with one SP. An orphan continuation is invalid." ✓

Let me double check the unfolding semantics once more: "replace the line break and the maximal leading SP/HTAB run with one SP". So for:
```
Call-ID: abc
   def
```
The value becomes "abc" + " " + "def" = "abc def" ✓ (my implementation: fields[-1][1] + " " + line.lstrip(" \t")) ✓.

Note: the trailing whitespace of the continuation line is preserved in the middle of the value, and the final outer strip removes it only at the ends ✓.

"A new header has a nonempty token name, optional SP/HTAB, colon, and value." ✓

"Token characters are ASCII letters/digits and - . ! % * _ + ` ' ~ (the backtick between plus and apostrophe is itself a token character)." ✓ — my TOKEN_CHARS includes the backtick ✓. Let me double check the string: "-._!%*+`'~" — yes: - . _ ! % * + ` ' ~ ✓. All 9 ✓.

"Strip outer SP/HTAB from values after unfolding." ✓

"Names are case-insensitive." ✓

"Compact names f,t,i,l,c mean From, To, Call-ID, Content-Length, Content-Type respectively." ✓

"Exactly one each of From, To, Call-ID, CSeq, Content-Length is required." ✓

"At most one each of P-Preferred-Identity, Remote-Party-ID, Privacy, Content-Type is permitted." ✓

"Duplicates count after compact-name expansion." ✓

"P-Asserted-Identity may repeat; concatenate its address lists in arrival order." ✓

"Other fields may repeat; they have no semantics here and are discarded after header framing is checked." ✓

"A missing/duplicate required or optional singleton is syntax, even for equal values." ✓

"Call-ID matches [A-Za-z0-9_.@+-]{1,128}." ✓

"CSeq is decimal digits, one or more SP/HTAB, and the exact request method; its number is in 1..2147483647." ✓

"Content-Length is nonempty decimal digits (leading zeros permitted), and must equal the ASCII body length exactly." ✓

"Content-Type, if present, is a nonempty sequence of printable ASCII and HTAB; retain the unfolded, outer-trimmed value verbatim." ✓

"Privacy is id or none, case-insensitive. No other tokens or combinations." ✓

Everything checks out.

Now let me think about the "## Address grammar and normalization" once more:

"From and To contain exactly one address, with optional ;tag=TOKEN afterward."

Hmm — "with optional ;tag=TOKEN afterward". So the tag comes after the address ✓.

"Allow SP/HTAB around the semicolon and equals, and around the tag value."

Hmm, "around the tag value" — so `;tag= value ` — the value is trimmed ✓. My implementation skips whitespace after '=' and then takes the token run; trailing whitespace after the value is handled by the outer trim (or by the caller's skip_ws) ✓.

Hmm, wait: there's a subtlety. My implementation takes the token run and then returns pos = the end of the token run. If the tag value is followed by whitespace and then more text, e.g. ";tag=abc def", the leftover " def" → the caller (parse_single_address) requires the end → syntax ✓.

"Tag is case-sensitive, 1-128 token characters; the parameter name is case-insensitive." ✓

"No other header parameters are supported." ✓

"PPI, RPID and PAI addresses have no header parameters." ✓

"PPI and RPID contain exactly one address." ✓

"Total PAI addresses must be one or two, and if two, exactly one must be sip and the other tel." ✓

"These are cardinality/grammar rules, regardless of whether a claim is trusted." ✓

OK. Now let me finalize. Let me run all the tests one more time, verify the public check, check the file size and permissions.

And the output "Privacy: id" ✓.

One more: what if the Privacy header value is "Id" → "id" ✓.

Let me also double check: the output Privacy is "id" when private, which includes the case where the Privacy header was absent but the From was anonymous ✓.

Let me run the final tests.

Actually, one more important thing I should verify: the behavior when the same batch contains a job that sources a job whose wire contains characters that need JSON escaping ✓ (json.dumps handles it).

And: the output JSON must not contain NaN/Infinity ✓ (no floats).
